candidates: Add a TSDoc `/** */` block comment with `@param` tags to every newly exported function and to any constructor or method that gains a new parameter; callers should not need to read the implementation to understand the public API.

Prefer project-defined named type aliases (e.g. `Pick<DiagramMetadata, 'title'>`) over inline object literal types (e.g. `{title?: string}`) when the same shape appears in more than one function signature; using a shared type makes future changes propagate automatically and signals intentional reuse.

When extracting a function or module into a new file, preserve the original TypeScript parameter types rather than weakening them (e.g. do not change `args: unknown` to `args: any`); if loosening is genuinely required by the new context, justify it with an inline comment.

When test assertions are removed or modified (e.g. stripping out directive-related setup or assertions), update the `it()` description and any enclosing `describe()` block title to accurately reflect what the test now verifies; stale test names mislead future contributors about what is actually being covered.

Do not delete test spec files without confirming that all their test cases are covered elsewhere; if a file needs to be renamed (e.g. to add a `.js` or `.ts` extension), migrate all existing test cases, using `it.skip()` with an explanatory comment only for tests that are genuinely obsolete.
